details.recommendation: Citation count is adequate but quality ratio is low. Replace weaker sources with peer-reviewed or institutional references.

accuracy.notes: Most claims verified as accurate. PrimoGPT/PrimoRL performance metrics (58.47% return, 1.70 Sharpe) confirmed via MDPI paper. Riskfolio-Lib v7.2.1 with 24 risk measures confirmed. SR 11-7 details accurate. Minor issue: the 134.05% FinRL return was from the 2024 contest (LLM-RLMF task), not the 2025 DeepSeek task specifically. The Gartner '70% of enterprises' claim could not be independently verified from public sources. MLOps market size ($1.58B, 35.5% CAGR) confirmed via DataToBiz/Fortune Business Insights.

relevance.notes: All four research areas are highly relevant to the AI quantitative trading mission. Team 2 focused on the most impactful areas: ML trading SOTA, portfolio optimization tools, data infrastructure, and regulatory compliance. Strong practical orientation with tool comparisons and code examples.

citation_quality.notes: 38 total citations across 4 topics (9.5 avg) is strong in quantity. However, quality ratio is only 36.8% high-quality sources. Too many medium.com, blog, and commercial vendor pages vs peer-reviewed sources. Data infrastructure topic had ZERO high-quality citations. ML trading topic had the best citation quality (7/12 from arxiv, NeurIPS, Nature). Missing key academic sources: Gu/Kelly/Xiu 2020, Buehler et al. 2019, original SHAP/LIME papers.

depth.notes: Average 298.8 words per topic is solid (just under the A threshold of 300). Findings are well-structured with numbered sections. Each topic covers 5-7 distinct sub-areas. However, depth within individual techniques could be greater - most get 1-2 sentences rather than in-depth analysis of methodology, limitations, and real-world deployment challenges.

completeness.notes: Team 2 covered 4 areas deeply vs Team 1's 8 areas broadly. Missing from Team 2: alternative data, HFT, NLP/sentiment (separate from XAI), risk management as standalone topic. Within covered areas, some gaps: no discussion of overfitting/look-ahead bias risks in ML trading, no mention of transaction cost modeling in portfolio optimization, limited discussion of model drift in data infrastructure.

implementation_detail.notes: Strong practical focus with 9 code examples across 4 topics. Includes working snippets for PyPortfolioOpt, Riskfolio-Lib, skfolio, FinRL, TFT, Feast, MLflow, SHAP, and LIME. Tool comparison tables for portfolio libraries and feature stores. Version numbers provided (Riskfolio-Lib 7.2.1). This is Team 2's strongest dimension - significantly more implementation-ready than Team 1.

inaccuracies_found.claim: FinRL Contest 2025 top model achieved cumulative return of 134.05%
inaccuracies_found.correction: The 134.05% return was from the FinRL Contest 2024 LLM-RLMF task (Aethernet team using fine-tuned LLaMA-3.2-3B-Instruct), not the 2025 DeepSeek task. The 2025 contest had different tasks and results, including a 2nd place entry with 230.49% return using DAPO algorithm.

inaccuracies_found.claim: Gartner projects 70% of enterprises will operationalize AI architectures using MLOps
inaccuracies_found.correction: This specific claim could not be verified from public sources. The closest verifiable statistic is that 78% of enterprises worldwide deploy ML models in production (from industry reports, not Gartner specifically). The Gartner 70% figure may come from a gated report or may be conflated from other statistics.

Good specificity: concrete metrics throughout (Sharpe ratios, return percentages, latency figures, market sizes)
Practical orientation: code snippets that can be directly used by practitioners

team1_vs_team2.breadth_reasoning: Team 1 covered 8 distinct research areas (57 techniques) vs Team 2's 4 areas (42 techniques). Team 1 included alt data, HFT, NLP-sentiment, and risk management which Team 2 omitted entirely.
team1_vs_team2.depth_reasoning: Team 2 averaged 298.8 words per topic vs Team 1's 177.8 words. Team 2's findings include more structured detail within each area: numbered sub-sections, performance comparisons, and tool-level specifics.
team1_vs_team2.citation_quality_reasoning: Team 1 achieved 90% high-quality citation ratio (36/40 from arxiv, SSRN, IEEE, etc) vs Team 2's 36.8% (14/38). Team 1 cited original papers while Team 2 cited derivative blog posts. Team 1 grade: A. Team 2 grade: C.
team1_vs_team2.practical_utility_reasoning: Team 2 provided 9 working code examples with actual library imports vs Team 1's 11 GitHub links. Team 2's code is copy-paste ready (PyPortfolioOpt, Riskfolio-Lib, SHAP, etc.). Team 2 also provided direct tool comparisons and version numbers. Both scored A on specificity but Team 2's examples are more immediately actionable.
team1_vs_team2.reasoning: Team 1 wins overall due to superior breadth (8 vs 4 topics) and significantly better citation quality (90% vs 36.8% high-quality ratio). Both teams scored A on coverage and specificity. Team 2 excels in depth and practical implementation detail, making it more useful for practitioners, but the citation quality gap is substantial. Team 1's automated grade was A overall vs Team 2's B. For a comprehensive research survey, breadth and citation quality are more important than implementation depth. However, Team 2's contributions are complementary: its portfolio optimization tool comparisons, data infrastructure coverage, and regulatory detail fill gaps in Team 1's work. The ideal output combines Team 1's broad, well-cited foundation with Team 2's practical implementation focus.

verification_methodology.description: Manual verification conducted via web searches to spot-check specific claims, verify URL accessibility, confirm performance metrics, and identify missing sources.
